questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The life of Charles Darwin and his famous voyage
How to cure anxiety with medicine and therapy
The idea that anxiety evolved for a good reason
Why smoke alarms go off too often in kitchens
questions.why: Rob says anxiety may be a result of natural selection, and Dr Nesse explains why.

options: Not really, but he knows it's serious for some
Yes, every day, especially at work
Only before exams and job interviews
He refuses to talk about it on air
questions.why: He says 'Well not really, but I know for some people it can be quite a serious problem.'

questions.q: What puzzles Neil about anxiety and evolution?
options: Why animals don't feel anxiety
Why Darwin didn't write about it
Why it has become more common
Why such a negative feeling would develop
questions.why: He asks why develop anxiety when it 'seems like a negative rather than a positive thing'.

questions.q: How long did Dr Nesse treat patients at the University of Michigan?
options: 20 years
40 years
10 years
50 years
questions.why: He says, 'I treated patients with anxiety disorders for 40 years.'

questions.q: When did Dr Nesse realise anxiety exists for a good reason?
options: At the start of his career
At the very end of his career
About halfway through his career
When he read Darwin's work
questions.why: He says 'It was only half way through that I started realising.'

questions.q: According to Dr Nesse, what is anxiety?
options: A normal emergency response that helps in real danger
A disease caused by the stress of modern city life
A sign of weakness that people should learn to hide
A feeling that only humans have, not other animals
questions.why: He calls it 'a normal kind of emergency response which is great in life-threatening situations'.

questions.q: Why does Dr Nesse compare too much anxiety to a smoke detector when you burn toast?
options: Anxiety is often caused by cooking and kitchens
Smoke is very bad for our mental health
The alarm should simply be switched off
It is a warning when there is no real danger
questions.why: He says for these patients it's 'a false alarm like a smoke detector'.

questions.q: How did many patients react to Dr Nesse's explanation?
options: They became more worried about their health
They felt they might not need his help after all
They asked him for stronger medicine instead
They didn't believe him and found other doctors
questions.why: They said, 'that makes perfect sense, I think I won't need your help after all.'
